Junior Access Management Infrastructure Engineer

Program: Army Global Unified Network (AGUN)
Location: Remote | Up to 10% Travel, *Please be advised that during the interview, you will be required to keep your camera on, and your interviewer will be taking your picture for identification purposes, if an offer letter is extended to you.

Clearance Required: Active DoD Secret
Citizenship: U.S. Citizenship Required

Help Secure the U.S. Army's Global Network!

Leidos is seeking a Junior Access Management Infrastructure Engineer to support the Army Global Unified Network (AGUN) Migration team.

In this role, you'll help secure and modernize the Army's global network by supporting Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, identity and access management, and enterprise infrastructure security.

You'll work with engineering and cybersecurity teams to manage user access, troubleshoot identity-related issues, improve security, and support infrastructure modernization.

What You'll Do

Support Active Directory (AD), Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD), and Identity Management (IDM) systems.
Assist with Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), Multifactor Authentication (MFA), and directory synchronization.
Support automated user provisioning, deprovisioning, and access management workflows.
Troubleshoot directory replication, Group Policy, account access, and identity security issues.
Support Linux systems, virtualization, and container infrastructure.
Perform infrastructure patching, upgrades, configuration management, and security hardening.
Implement and validate DoD cybersecurity requirements and STIGs.
Support network monitoring, systems integration, testing, and migration activities.
Maintain identity management reports, configuration records, and technical documentation.
Collaborate with engineering, cybersecurity, and operations teams to resolve technical issues.

What We're Looking For

Required Qualifications

Active DoD Secret clearance and U.S. citizenship.
Bachelor's degree in a related technical field with 2–4 years of relevant experience, or a master's degree with 3 years of relevant experience. Additional applicable experience may be considered in place of a degree.
DoD IAT Level II certification (Security+ or equivalent) and an approved Computing Environment (CE) certification.
Experience supporting enterprise infrastructure, network management, or systems administration.
Strong troubleshooting, communication, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to work independently on routine assignments and collaborate with senior engineers.
Flexibility to work nonstandard shifts and travel up to 10%.

Required Technologies & Technical Skills

Identity & Access Management: Experience with Active Directory, Entra ID, or comparable identity management systems.
Access Security: Familiarity with RBAC, MFA, Group Policy, and identity lifecycle management.
Linux: Basic administration, configuration, and troubleshooting.
Networking: Understanding of LAN/WAN, TCP/IP, routing, and switching.
Virtualization: VMware, KVM, or comparable technologies.
Containers: Familiarity with Docker or Kubernetes.
Network Monitoring: Familiarity with ELK or comparable monitoring platforms.
Network Management: Experience with at least one of Palo Alto Panorama, Cisco Prime, Cisco DNA, or Junos Space.
Security: Knowledge of DoD STIGs, system hardening, and infrastructure security.

Preferred Qualifications & Technologies

Experience supporting U.S. Army, DISA, or other DoD networks.
Network+, CCNA, Red Hat certification, or equivalent.
Hands-on experience with Active Directory, Entra ID, identity governance, and access automation.
Experience with RHEL, Red Hat Satellite, VMware, vSAN, or Kubernetes.
Knowledge of ELK, InfoVista, or SIEM platforms.
Experience with Git, GitLab, Ansible, Terraform, Puppet, or Salt.
PowerShell, Python, or similar scripting for identity and infrastructure automation.
Familiarity with PKI, certificate management, and secure authentication technologies.
Experience supporting Windows Server, Dell servers, or enterprise infrastructure.
Experience with network migration, systems integration, and modernization.

Why Join Leidos?

At Leidos, you'll gain experience with enterprise identity and access management technologies while supporting the modernization of the U.S. Army's global communications infrastructure.

If you're a cleared Systems or Infrastructure Engineer with Active Directory, identity management, and infrastructure security experience, we'd like to hear from you!

Join Leidos and help secure the Army's global network. Apply today!

If you're looking for comfort, keep scrolling. At Leidos, we outthink, outbuild, and outpace the status quo — because the mission demands it. We're not hiring followers. We're recruiting the ones who disrupt, provoke, and refuse to fail. Step 10 is ancient history. We're already at step 30 — and moving faster than anyone else dares.

About Us
Leidos

For more information, visit  www.Leidos.com.

Pay and Benefits

Pay and benefits are fundamental to any career decision. That's why we craft compensation packages that reflect the importance of the work we do for our customers. Employment benefits include competitive compensation, Health and Wellness programs, Income Protection, Paid Leave and Retirement. More details are available here.

Securing Your Data

Leidos will never ask you to provide payment-related information at any part of the employment application process. And Leidos will communicate with you only through emails that are sent from a Leidos.com email address. If you receive an email purporting to be from Leidos that asks for payment-related information or any other personal information, please report the email to spam.leidos@leidos.com.
